articles.title: Abóbora gigante de 1.432 kg colhida nos EUA pode bater recorde mundial | G1
articles.standfirst: Fruto gigante foi colhido pelo produtor rural Ron Wallace, de Rhode Island, e pesado no sábado (10), durante uma competição na região da Nova Inglaterra. Vários concursos de abóboras gigantes acontecem neste mês e tem até premiação da mais bonita.
articles.summary: Fruto gigante foi colhido pelo produtor rural Ron Wallace, de Rhode Island, e pesado no sábado (10), durante uma competição na região da Nova Inglaterra.
articles.body:
Uma abóbora de 1.432 kg foi colhida nos Estados Unidos e pode ser reconhecida pelo Guinness, o Livro dos Recordes, como a mais pesada do mundo.

Ela foi cultivada pelo produtor rural Ron Wallace, do estado de Rhode Island, e pesada no sábado (10), durante um concurso de abóboras gigantes realizado no sul da região da Nova Inglaterra, nos EUA.

Wallace agora aguarda a confirmação do Guinness. O recorde atual pertence a uma abóbora de 1.296 kg cultivada por Ian Paton, de Lymington, na Inglaterra, e foi estabelecido em 3 de outubro — uma semana antes da pesagem da abóbora americana.

“Ela é realmente gigantesca. Foi um prazer cultivá-la”, disse Wallace por telefone, na segunda-feira (12).

Abóbora gigante de 1.432 quilos colhida nos EUA pode bater recorde mundial. — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram/@northeastgiantpumpkin

Wallace recebeu US$ 3.500 pela vitória na competição local. Ele contou que organizadores de outros concursos tentaram atraí-lo com prêmios maiores, alguns de até US$ 70 mil, mas que, para ele, era importante estar cercado pelas pessoas de sua comunidade no momento da vitória histórica.

“Fiquei eufórico. O lugar inteiro explodiu de alegria”, disse Wallace, ao descrever o momento em que a abóbora foi pesada.

Wallace atribui parte do resultado à troca de dicas e técnicas entre os produtores de abóboras gigantes. Neste ano, pela primeira vez, ele passou a cultivá-las em uma estufa, o que, segundo ele, fez uma grande diferença.

“A única maneira de produzir uma abóbora de mais de 1.360 kg é com uma comunidade trabalhando em conjunto”, afirmou.

Ele começou a cultivar abóboras por hobby depois de abrir uma loja virtual de produtos de jardinagem. Para Wallace, as competições ajudam a valorizar o trabalho dos produtores, que têm sido cada vez mais procurados pelo setor agrícola para orientar sobre o manejo do solo e outras técnicas de cultivo.

Travis Gienger, de Anoka, Minnesota, posa para foto com sua abóbora, vencedora do Campeonato Mundial de Pesagem de Abóboras Safeway, na segunda-feira, 12 de outubro de 2026, em Half Moon Bay, na Califórnia. — Foto: AP Photo/Jeff Chiu

A possível quebra do recorde acontece em meio a um mês de competições entre produtores de abóboras de vários países.

Na Califórnia, por exemplo, uma abóbora de 1.083 kg apelidada de "Rocky" venceu, na segunda-feira (12), um tradicional concurso de pesagem em Half Moon Bay, ao sul de São Francisco. O peso garantiu a vitória na competição, mas ficou longe do recorde mundial.

Cultivada pelo professor de horticultura Travis Gienger, a abóbora foi transportada em uma viagem de 35 horas, de Minnesota até a Califórnia. Ele superou dezenas de concorrentes, conquistou seu quinto título e recebeu um prêmio de US$ 21.501.

Travis Gienger, de Anoka, Minnesota, comemora a vitória de sua abóbora, com o peso exibido no painel acima, no Campeonato Mundial de Pesagem de Abóboras Safeway, na segunda-feira, 12 de outubro de 2026, em Half Moon Bay, na Califórnia. — Foto: AP Photo/Jeff Chiu

No ano passado, Gienger ficou fora da disputa porque sua abóbora rachou enquanto crescia. Para marcar o retorno à competição, batizou a deste ano de Rocky, em homenagem ao boxeador interpretado por Sylvester Stallone.

“Pentacampeão. Foi isso que viemos buscar”, disse Gienger, após a vitória.

Gienger e sua família passaram 35 horas na estrada até chegar à Califórnia, levando uma abóbora do tamanho de um carro pequeno.

O professor cultiva as abóboras no quintal de casa, em Anoka, às margens do rio Mississippi, ao norte de Minneapolis. Neste ano, teve de lidar com temperaturas abaixo de zero. Para melhorar o desempenho nas disputas, Gienger acredita que terá de passar a cultivar as abóboras em um ambiente com temperatura controlada, como faz Wallace.

“É impressionante que Travis consiga enfrentar condições climáticas adversas, como temperaturas de cerca de −1 °C, e ainda assim cultivar uma abóbora desse tamanho”, disse o organizador da competição, Ronan Fowler.

A abóbora Tinker Bell, eleita a mais bonita, é pesada no Campeonato Mundial de Pesagem de Abóboras Safeway, na segunda-feira, 12 de outubro de 2026, em Half Moon Bay, na Califórnia. — Foto: AP/Jeff Chiu

A 53ª edição do Campeonato Mundial de Pesagem de Abóboras reuniu centenas de pessoas, com comida, música e até piadas sobre abóboras.

O público também vibrou com a vitória de Tinkerbell — Sininho, em português —, que conquistou o título de mais bonita graças ao formato bastante simétrico.

A premiação foi de cerca de US$ 19,84 por quilo de abóbora. Gienger ficou sem o bônus de US$ 30 mil reservado a quem quebrasse o recorde mundial, mas sua campeã será uma das atrações de um desfile em Half Moon Bay neste fim de semana.

Quem esperava uma torta gigante, porém, ficou na vontade: essas abóboras são cultivadas para impressionar pelo tamanho, não pelo sabor.

Miles, de 6 anos, passa dirigindo ao lado de uma abóbora gigante que será inscrita no Campeonato Mundial de Pesagem de Abóboras Safeway, na segunda-feira, 12 de outubro de 2026, em Half Moon Bay, na Califórnia. — Foto: Jeff Chiu/AP

articles.title: Anac registra 57 casos de indisciplina no 1º mês de regra que pune má conduta de passageiros | G1
articles.standfirst: Entre os casos registrados desde 14 de setembro, houve um episódio considerado gravíssimo e 15 ocorrências graves; todos ainda estão sob análise da agência.
articles.summary: Entre os casos registrados desde 14 de setembro, houve um episódio considerado gravíssimo e 15 ocorrências graves; todos ainda estão sob análise da agência.
articles.body:
O setor aéreo brasileiro registrou 57 casos de indisciplina de passageiros no primeiro mês de vigência da regra que prevê punições para condutas inadequadas dentro dos aviões ou nos aeroportos do país. A média foi de quase dois casos por dia.

Os números são da Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac) e foram obtidos pela TV Globo. A resolução que pune passageiros indisciplinados começou a valer em 14 de setembro.

Nesse período, foi registrado apenas um caso considerado gravíssimo: um atentado à dignidade sexual praticado por um passageiro no dia 18 de setembro , durante um voo entre Belém e Campinas.

O regulamento pune os casos gravíssimos com multa de R$ 17,5 mil e a suspensão do direito de voar por período que vai de seis meses a um ano.

De acordo com a Anac, todos os casos de indisciplina registrados até o momento ainda estão sob análise , ou seja, nenhum passageiro teve a punição confirmada de maneira definitiva.

articles.title: How Much You Need to Retire Comfortably With a Paid-Off Home in Every State
articles.summary: How much retirement savings do you need if your home is paid off? See the nest egg required for singles and couples in every state, based on living costs.
articles.body:
A single retiree with a paid-off home needs about $693,000 in savings, on average, to retire comfortably, though the amount varies by state.

A typical mortgage-free couple would need about $870,000 on average.

Even without a mortgage, retirees still face housing costs, including property taxes, insurance, maintenance, and utilities.

Paying off your mortgage before you retire can feel like clearing one of the biggest hurdles keeping you from . Take away that monthly payment, and you may need far less of a nest egg.

But that doesn't mean you won't have housing bills—insurance, utilities, property taxes, maintenance, and other living expenses don't disappear. These expenses vary by address, which is why an Investopedia analysis of federal data finds that geography makes a big difference in how much you need to retire comfortably.

How Much Mortgage-Free Retirees Need to Save

Almost 80% of U.S. households headed by someone 65 or older own their home, and of those, close to two-thirds own it free and clear.

A single retiree with a paid-off home needs about $693,000 in savings to retire comfortably, according to Investopedia's analysis. Depending on the state, that figure ranges from about $572,000 to $909,000.

Meanwhile, a typical mortgage-free couple needs about $870,000 in savings for a comfortable retirement. Depending on where they choose to live, the estimate ranges from about $700,000 to $1.18 million.

Those mortgage-free estimates are well below the $1.46 million Americans told Northwestern Mutual this year they'd need to retire comfortably. Unlike Investopedia's calculations, however, that figure reflects what survey respondents believe they'll need, rather than an estimate based on retirement expenses.

One big reason our estimates are lower is that retirees free of a mortgage payment have a significant cost advantage, with of $658 for households headed by someone age 65 or older, versus $1,736 for owners still paying off a mortgage, according to Census data.

Retirement savings targets that are one-size-fits-all can miss how much a change in housing costs shifts the math. Where you live and whether you've paid off your mortgage can mean needing to save far less to retire comfortably.

Where a Paid-Off Home Stretches Retirement Savings Furthest

Investopedia's model estimates the cost of a comfortable year of retirement in each state, including everyday spending and the housing costs homeowners still face after the mortgage is gone.

articles.summary: Gold held a two-day decline after a Federal Reserve official signaled one more interest-rate hike may be needed this year, but further tightening won’t be ne...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Gold held a two-day decline after a Federal Reserve official signaled one more interest-rate hike may be needed this year, but further tightening won't be necessary in 2027, improving sentiment toward the precious metal.

Bullion traded near $4,155 an ounce, after falling 0.8% in the previous two sessions. Oil rose as a flare-up in attacks in the Middle East threatened further energy disruptions that could weigh on inflation and make a case for higher borrowing costs. Brent crude was above $106 a barrel.

Fed New York President John Williams said he sees one more interest-rate hike as appropriate this year. US Treasury yields edged lower after his remarks, supporting gold, which typically does better in a lower rate environment as it doesn't pay interest.

US consumer price index data due later on Wednesday may provide clues on the Fed's rate path, after it hiked for the first time since 2023 last month. Swaps traders are pricing in a low chance of a rise at this month's policy meeting, but see a roughly 90% chance of an increase in December.

Spot gold dipped 0.1% to $4,157.37 an ounce at 8:05 a.m. Singapore time, while silver was 0.2% lower at $59.04. Platinum fell 0.4% and palladium was little changed. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index, a gauge of the US currency, was flat after slipping 0.2% in the previous session.

articles.title: Rollout of BS-VII in 3 phases from April 2029 to April 2035
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Govt is all set to roll out BS-VII emission standards, aligned with Euro 7 norms, in phases, starting April 2029.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Govt is all set to roll out BS-VII emission standards, aligned with Euro 7 norms, in phases, starting April 2029. The new norms will set stricter limits on harmful pollutants, including nitrogen oxides, hydrocarbons and particulate matter amid heightened pollution risks across Indian cities.BS-VII will start with new cars and SUVs manufactured from April 2029, followed by small goods delivery and pick-up vans from 2030 and buses and heavy-duty vehicles from April 2031. The new norms for two-wheelers - the biggest contributor to pollution - will, however, be notified later.Unlike BS-VI, which was first rolled out from April 2020, it will not require changes in the refinery infrastructure to produce petrol and diesel suitable for the upgraded emission standards, officials said. It will, however, require the automobile sector to upgrade engines.TOI has learnt that the road transport ministry has approved the proposed timeline, and draft notifications for the three categories of vehicles are expected over the next few days. The proposed emission norms will not affect existing vehicles or their life, including those compliant with BS-VI standards.The proposed standards will strengthen emissions monitoring beyond controlled laboratory tests to ensure vehicles comply with prescribed limits under real-world driving conditions and throughout their operational life. The implementation of all the new norms will be in three phases spanning six years - April 2029 to April 2035 - giving adequate time to industry and testing agencies.According to the finalised norms, the cut-off limits of various emission components for cars and SUVs remain unchanged compared with BS-VI. Particulate number has, however, been reduced fr-om 23 nanometres to 10 nanometres, resulting in improved filtration of pollutants. Smaller particles penetrate deeper into lungs. A person aware of the matter said the proposed change makes the regulation more stringent by capturing ultrafine particles, which have been unregulated thus far.The transition from BS-VI to BS-VII will have more impact on trucks and heavy-duty vehicles, with the proposed standard aimed at reducing emissions in the range of 20-50% across pollutants. This will be more stringent for on-road emissions.People involved in framing the norms said BS-VII goes beyond tailpipe emission by regulating non-exhaust sources such as brake wear and tyre abrasion. Moreover, the new norms will introduce the concept of market surveillance, where independent testing agencies will conduct in-use compliance checks.Officials said the norms are fully aligned with Euro 7 and its implementation, which was also structured in a phased manner, starting Nov 2026 for light-duty vehicles and May 2028 for heavy-duty vehicles. The full rollout will extend up to 2035.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: More adult nappies, more pet prams? What Japan and Korea’s numbers really say
articles.summary: Two small objects offer a striking glimpse of demographic change in Japan and South Korea: a nappy and a pram.
articles.body: Two small objects offer a striking glimpse of demographic change in Japan and South Korea: a nappy and a pram. But the numbers behind them answer different questions.In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. That is a comparison by number of pieces. The adult count includes pads and liners as well as nappies and pants. It measures production, which is not necessarily the same as the number bought or used in Japan.South Korea’s 2025 finding looks similar at first: 61,418 tonnes of adult products supplied, compared with 54,001 tonnes of child products. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. But a heavier pile need not contain more nappies. Both Korean categories also include hygiene underpads.How different might the count be? One Japanese study calculated an average weight of 62.4g for an adult nappy and 32.1g for a baby nappy. Applying those weights to Korea’s supply gives the following illustration, not an estimate of actual Korean sales:Those weights come from Japan and do not account for the mix of products in Korea’s supply. They cannot establish Korea’s actual piece count. They do show why the distinction matters: adult supply weighs about 14% more, yet could comprise fewer individual products. For adult products to lead by number, their average weight would have to be less than about 14% greater than the child average.The pram finding has a different boundary. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales by number through September 2024; baby strollers accounted for 42%. The result describes sales on Gmarket. It does not tell us which type sold more across every shop in South Korea, or how many homes have pets and children.The three figures are revealing when read precisely: Japan’s adult products lead by pieces produced; Korea’s adult products lead by weight supplied; and pet strollers led on Gmarket. Each captures part of a changing market. The unit and the source determine exactly what we can say about it.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Singapore’s economy grows more than 5 percent amid AI boom
articles.summary: City-state’s GDP expands 5.4 percent in July-September quarter, according to advance government estimates.
articles.body:
Singapore’s economy grew more than 5 percent in the most recent quarter, continuing an AI-fuelled boom that has made the city-state one of the fastest-growing advanced economies.

Gross domestic product (GDP) grew 5.4 percent year-on-year between July and September, down from a 6.2 percent expansion in the second quarter, according to advance government estimates released on Wednesday.

Manufacturing, which is dominated by the city-state’s semiconductor industry, grew 7.5 percent, according to the estimates from the Ministry of Trade and Industry.

Increased output in “electronics, precision engineering, transport engineering and general manufacturing clusters” drove growth, the ministry said, offsetting declines in the chemicals and biomedical sectors.

Construction, including AI-related investments such as data centres, expanded 8.8 per cent, according to the figures.

Despite the heady expansion, Singapore’s central bank left its monetary policy settings untouched in its latest announcement on Wednesday, citing expectations that AI demand will cool in 2027.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore, which manages monetary policy through currency exchange rates rather than interest rates, said it expected core inflation to average 1.5–2.0 percent in 2026.

“Global AI-driven growth is expected to ease in the latter half of next year from its current exceptional pace, while higher interest rates, amid elevated inflation in the advanced economies, would weigh on final demand growth,” the central bank said in a statement.

Singapore is a major global player in the booming chip sector, a position that has helped it weather choppy economic conditions, including the energy shock prompted by the US-Israel war on Iran.

The Southeast Asian city-state accounts for roughly 10 percent of global semiconductor output and 20 percent of semiconductor equipment production, according to government figures.

Yeow Hwee Chua, an assistant professor of economics at Nanyang Technological University, described Singapore’s economic performance as “impressive for a high-income economy, especially given the uncertain global environment”.

“The global technology investment boom has been an important driver,” Chua told Al Jazeera.

“Strong demand for electronics has supported manufacturing and related wholesale trade, illustrating how Singapore benefits from its position in global supply chains,” he said.

Singapore’s economy is expected to grow 5 percent in 2026, according to the IMF’s latest economic forecast, faster than any other advanced economy except Taiwan.

The city-state’s GDP grew 5 percent in 2025, its second straight year of growth above 5 percent – the first such streak since 2010 and 2011.

articles.title: Man jointly bought Rs 80 lakh property with father and wife but didn't file ITR; taxman added Rs 55.2 lakh as unexplained money, but ITAT grants relief after proof of family contributions
articles.summary: A man bought a residential property along with his wife and father. However, he did not file his income tax return for the year.
articles.body: A man bought a residential property along with his wife and father. However, he did not file his income tax return for the year.The tax department opened his case for reassessment and adding Rs 55.2 lakh as unexplained investment. The Mumbai bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) deleted the Rs 55.2 lakh addition made to a taxpayer's income. Here’s what the case is about:What the case is aboutA man bought a residential property jointly with his wife and his father. The Income Tax Department reopened his assessment for the 2016-17 assessment year after receiving information through its Risk Management Strategy that he had purchased an immovable property during the 2015-16 financial year. The assessment proceedings recorded that he had not filed an income tax return for the relevant year.Also Read | Wife sold shares for Rs 8.31 crore LTCG, bought husband’s Mumbai property for Rs 7.5 crore and claimed Section 54F exemption; taxman calls it tax avoidance, but ITAT Mumbai gives relief to herDuring reassessment, the man explained that the property had been funded through several sources, including a Rs 32 lakh housing loan from a bank and contributions from himself and his family members. The assessing officer accepted the housing loan but considered that the remaining investment was insufficiently explained.The officer calculated the addition using total payments of Rs 87.2 lakh and deducted the accepted housing loan of Rs 32 lakh, treating the balance of Rs 55.2 lakh as unexplained investment under Section 69 of the Income Tax Act, read with Section 115BBE.The National Faceless Appeal Centre upheld the addition. It found that the evidence submitted at that stage did not adequately establish the sources of the contributions attributed to the man’s father and wife.The man then approached the ITAT, challenging both the addition and the calculation underlying it. He argued that the property was jointly owned and that the payments had come from identifiable sources. He also disputed the assessing officer’s use of Rs 87.2 lakh, contending that the actual payments, including VAT, were Rs 84 lakh.Before the tribunal, the man submitted additional documents, including bank statements, employment and remuneration records, and material relating to his father’s pension and funds.Also Read | Delhi couple repaid Rs 1.41 crore home loan, but the bank lost their original sale deed property papers; consumer commission orders Rs 15 lakh compensation plus Rs 50,000 costsWhy did ITAT delete the tax additions?The bench examined the additional evidence submitted by the man, including banking records and documents concerning the family members’ financial contributions.It found that the payments towards the property could be identified and were supported by documentary material. The evidence also established that the property had been purchased jointly, rather than solely by the man.According to the judgement, the assessee explained the sources towards the acquisition as a housing loan of Rs 32,00,000/-, contribution by his father of Rs 11,20,000/-, contribution by his wife of Rs 20,00,000/-, his own funds of Rs 1,70,000/- and further funds of Rs 19,10,000/-.The tribunal considered the housing loan, the taxpayer’s own funds and the contributions attributed to his wife and father in the context of the records placed before it.The significance of the additional evidence was that it addressed the gaps in the explanation that the lower authorities had relied on when making and sustaining the addition.Also Read | Son claimed share in mother’s Delhi house, saying he paid Rs 1.5 lakh for land and Rs 60,000 for construction; Delhi High Court rejects claim, orders him and wife to vacateThe calculation of the investment was another important issue. The agreed consideration recorded for the property was Rs 80 lakh. The man contended that actual payments, including VAT, were Rs 84 lakh, while the assessing officer had used Rs 87.2 lakh to calculate the unexplained investment.The tribunal found that the higher figure adopted by the assessing officer was not substantiated by the documents on record. The discrepancy mattered because the Rs 55.2 lakh addition had been calculated by deducting the accepted housing loan from the higher payment figure.The tribunal held that the investment could not be treated as unexplained in the manner adopted by the assessing officer.The tribunal therefore deleted the Rs 55.2 lakh addition under Section 69 read with Section 115BBE.According to Raghav Bajaj, Partner at Khaitan & Co, the ruling restates an important principle: Section 69 is not a tool for presumptive attribution.Before an investment can be taxed as unexplained, it must first be established that the taxpayer has made an investment, and only then ask whether its source has been satisfactorily explained.The immovable property was bought jointly by a son, his father and his wife. It was financed through a joint housing loan and paid for through traceable bank transfers from each of their accounts.“Despite this, the entire balance was attributed to one co-owner by the tax officer. The Tribunal held that an addition built on assumption, and on numbers that cannot be reconciled with the actual payments evidenced by documents, is not valid,” Bajaj explains.Also Read | Woman declared Rs 67.4 lakh ancestral jewellery in her ITR which led to additions by tax department; ITAT Mumbai deleted it on basis of old records, but rejected her Rs 12 lakh HUF brokerage claimSignificance of rulingThe decision matters well beyond its facts. Pooling salaries, pensions, savings and inherited funds to buy a home is a familiar reality for Indian families, and this ruling recognises each such contributor's role, Bajaj tells TOI.At the same time, the case is a cautionary tale – taxpayers should keep a clear, person-wise record of contributions from the day of purchase in similar facts.“Further, it must also be noted that analytics-led reassessments are a legitimate and efficient way to identify high-value transactions, but a data flag is the beginning of an inquiry, not its conclusion. Where title is shared, each co-owner's sources must be examined on their own merits, and any addition must be confined to the share genuinely left unexplained,” Bajaj adds.However, according to him, one significant question remains open. The taxpayer also challenged the validity of the reopening itself, arguing that the income that could have escaped assessment did not exceed the Rs 50 lakh threshold relevant to the limitation provisions.“Having decided the case on merits, the Tribunal did not rule on that point. Taxpayers facing similar reassessments should therefore raise and preserve jurisdictional challenges from the outset, alongside a well-documented defence on merits,” he says.Also Read | Man enters JDA for land, gets 6 flats from builder and transfers 5 to wife, but gets tax notice; ITAT Delhi deletes Rs 4.14 crore additions after finding no stock-in-trade conversion or saleYou use AI every day. articles.title: Grab announces new Thailand initiative with OpenAI
articles.summary: Southeast Asia’s multi-purpose app Grab will work with OpenAI to boost the AI skills of its drivers, sellers and other providers in Thailand, the Singapore-based company announced on Wednesday.
articles.body: Southeast Asia’s multi-purpose app Grab will work with OpenAI to boost the AI skills of its drivers, sellers and other providers in Thailand, the Singapore-based company announced on Wednesday. The joint program plans to train 3,000 Grab gig workers across Thailand to tap into new sources of income through a series of practical AI workshops. Participants will also receive three months of free ChatGPT Plus access. “Giving accessibility is just one thing. It’s how do you translate it again to earnings to their pocket, upskilling, reskilling every one of them, and that’s why today I’m here in Thailand,” Grab CEO Anthony Tan said in an exclusive announcement at CNN’s Global Perspectives event in Bangkok. Workshops will be delivered through the Grab Driver App. Featured training topics include customer engagement and retention, marketing and branding, personal finance and first aid. Grab began as a ride-hailing service and later expanded into food delivery, digital payments and business solutions for local small businesses. The regional tech giant operates in eight countries and over 900 cities across Southeast Asia. The “GO Forward with AI” launch in Thailand is part of a broader partnership with OpenAI that aims to upskill over 30,000 gig workers and entrepreneurs across the region over the next two years. The initiative was first announced by Grab and OpenAI last month. Beginning in Singapore, it was subsequently expanded to Thailand and was said to be launching in Indonesia and the Philippines later this year, according to the companies’ statements. Through the AI training provided, Grab envisions that participants would be able to tap AI agentic capabilities – such as delegating multi-step tasks, building simple websites and creating repeatable workflows – beyond asking one-off questions. “Our partners are intrigued by AI, and many are looking for practical guidance on how to apply it in ways that are relevant to their work, businesses and aspirations,” said Ong Chin Yin, Grab’s chief organizational capability officer, in the September statement. “This program is about building that confidence – whether it’s helping a merchant make smarter business decisions or giving a driver-partner the tools to explore a new business idea and create new opportunities for growth,” she added. “As we enter a new era of AI capabilities, it’s not enough for people to simply have access to AI. They also need the skills and confidence to use it, adapt as the technology changes, and share in the progress it creates,” said Kiran Mani, OpenAI’s Asia Pacific managing director, in a Wednesday statement. “People across Thailand are already embracing AI, and through GO Forward with AI, we’re excited to work with Grab to turn that interest into practical skills,” he added. Grab has partnered with OpenAI since 2024, launching several AI applications, including its in-app Driver AI Assistant that it says has reached over half a million drivers and helped them find demand, optimize earnings and resolve day-to-day questions.

articles.title: ECB President Christine Lagarde signals no intervention in France’s fiscal crisis
articles.summary: The president of the European Central Bank played down speculation about intervention in France’s ballooning budget crisis on Wednesday.
articles.body: The president of the European Central Bank played down speculation about intervention in France’s ballooning budget crisis on Wednesday. Asked whether there are plans for the ECB to step in, Christine Lagarde said the solution to the precarious financial state of the European Union’s second-largest economy would be domestic. “There are particular circumstances that lead to some countries being more affected, France being a case in point,” she told the CNN Global Perspectives event in Bangkok. “For that one, the primary and first solution lies at home in France, and it has to do with fiscal policies.” France has been embroiled in a rapidly escalating public debt crisis that risks dragging the EU down with it. The financial pressure rapidly snowballed in recent weeks as bond yields spike and unprecedented student protests rock the country. Public debt has reached nearly 120% of GDP, while the benchmark 10-year bond yields surged to nearly 5% – the highest level in more than two decades – pushing up borrowing costs and slowing economic activity. All this, coupled with the country’s high social welfare spending, leaves the government little room for maneuver, let alone to address the demands of students, who want solutions to staff shortages and dilapidated school buildings. Investors are also concerned that efforts to reduce the deficit may be hampered, with a presidential election coming next year. Lagarde, however, also highlighted that rising bond yields are not unique to France. Bond yields in major economies such as the United States, Germany and Japan have all jumped in recent weeks, as a result of a confluence of factors including rising government debt and a prolonged energy shock caused by the Iran war.

articles.title: Why Gen Z needs a different approach to education
articles.summary: For generations, education followed a predictable path. Learn what is taught, complete a degree, find a job and build a career.
articles.body: For generations, education followed a predictable path. Learn what is taught, complete a degree, find a job and build a career. But Gen Z is entering a world where artificial intelligence, automation and evolving skill requirements are reshaping that journey.I believe education must respond by combining strong academic foundations with the ability to apply knowledge in unfamiliar situations.Information is available almost instantly. Students can access lectures, research and practical demonstrations from across the world. The greater educational challenge is helping them interpret that information, question assumptions and use it well. My experience in management education has reinforced a simple principle: students need opportunities to apply, experiment, reflect and improve throughout their studies.Measure learning through capabilityCompleting a syllabus does not necessarily mean a student can analyse a business problem, communicate an idea or lead a team. We need to judge education by the capabilities students develop, alongside the knowledge they acquire.Outcome-based education provides a framework for this shift. It asks what students should be able to demonstrate after a course, then connects teaching and assessment to those outcomes. In management education, these may include analytical thinking, financial understanding, communication and effective teamwork.I have emphasised internships, corporate interaction and project-based learning throughout my academic leadership. Case studies, simulations and live projects give concepts a practical context. They also allow students to encounter problems without a single textbook answer. Academic rigour becomes more meaningful when students can use it to explain a decision or develop a solution.Recognise the individual learnerStudents bring different strengths, interests and ambitions to the classroom. Some are drawn to entrepreneurship; others excel in analysis or communication. Many need support in identifying a career direction.Personalised learning does not require a separate curriculum for every student. It requires attention to the individual behind the qualification. Mentoring, career counselling, psychometric assessment and development tailored to a student’s profile can help them understand their strengths and make informed choices. Education should help students explore the professionals they could become, as well as the degrees they can complete.Teach students to think with technologyAdding AI or robotics to a curriculum is only a starting point. Students also need to understand how technology affects business models, professional decisions and careers.When a tool generates an answer, the learner must still judge whether the question was useful, the answer is sound and the application is appropriate. Critical thinking, creativity, communication and ethical reasoning therefore belong at the centre of technology education.My research and academic work1 2 3 increasingly intersect with digital transformation and emerging technologies. That experience reinforces my view that technical familiarity must be accompanied by judgement. Students need to understand how to think with technology and use it responsibly.Develop initiative and global capabilityEntrepreneurship education extends beyond starting a company. It develops the habit of identifying problems, testing solutions, accepting uncertainty and creating value. I have advocated for students to become creators of opportunities. That mindset is equally useful within an established organisation, where an employee may spot a problem and develop a better way of working.Global exposure also needs a clear educational purpose. Travel alone cannot create global competence. Students need opportunities to understand different markets, cultures and ways of thinking through exchanges, international collaborations and cross-cultural projects.In my academic leadership experience, international partnerships have created opportunities for student and faculty exchanges, joint programmes and collaborative research. Their educational value lies in helping participants work across differences and apply what they learn in a globally connected environment.Prepare students to keep learningA graduate’s first job may not define their eventual career. As industries and roles evolve, the knowledge gained at the beginning of working life will need to be revisited. Education must develop the confidence and habits to learn, unlearn and relearn.This requires classrooms that remain connected to the world outside them. Real business problems, industry interaction and opportunities to experiment should be part of the learning experience. Strong conceptual knowledge provides the foundation; practical experience helps students test and deepen their understanding.I believe educators must ask whether our education systems are ready for the students we teach. Our responsibility is to develop people who can think independently, apply knowledge and continue learning long after graduation. For Gen Z, that is the educational experience we need to build.This article has been contributed by Dr. Amol Gawande, Director of Brookstone Institute of Global Studies, Dubai, and an Executive Board Member of the Association of Indian Management Schools (AIMS)References:Digital Transformation and Consumer Behaviour (2025): Machine Learning Algorithms (2021), listed in the institutional publication records: ResearchGate academic profile: These references document his contributions to technology-related academic publications and research.Disclaimer: The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.You use AI every day. articles.title: KL University and KLH Hyderabad campuses enter the agentic AI era
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence is moving beyond chatbots and content generation, with autonomous systems increasingly capable of reasoning, planning and
articles.body: Artificial intelligence is moving beyond chatbots and content generation, with autonomous systems increasingly capable of reasoning, planning and executing tasks. KL Deemed to be University and KLH Hyderabad are bringing this next phase of AI into higher education through a new partnership with HCL Group AI Labs*, with its Agentic AI Campus initiative taking shape across its academic ecosystem, including its Vaddeswaram and Hyderabad campuses.The initiative, also unveiled at KLH Hyderabad, will integrate AI and agentic technologies into academic programmes, laboratories, projects and day-to-day learning, with AI-focused degrees also planned.The partnership is built around a broader shift in how students engage with technology. Rather than limiting AI to a standalone subject, the university plans to embed it across disciplines and enable students to progress from using AI tools to designing and deploying intelligent systems.Students will be introduced to machine learning, generative AI, large language models and agentic architectures, alongside practical capabilities such as prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, multimodal applications, intelligent chatbots, AI copilots, enterprise assistants, intelligent search and decision-support systems.The curriculum will also connect these emerging capabilities with core software skills, including programming, full-stack development, cloud computing, databases, DevOps and application deployment. This combination is intended to help students understand not only how AI systems work, but also how to build, integrate and operate them in real-world environments.“AI is transforming how industries operate, innovate and create value, and universities must embed it across the learning ecosystem rather than treat it as a single subject,” said Koneru Satyanarayana, Chancellor, KL Deemed to be University. “Working with HCL AI Labs, we want students across disciplines to move from using AI tools to designing,” he adds.According to Srinath, Dean – Student Skilling and Progression, the programme will use project-based learning to translate classroom concepts into working applications. Students will tackle use cases spanning healthcare, education, agriculture, manufacturing, finance, retail, cybersecurity, smart cities, human resources and enterprise automation.Industry-led problem statements, hackathons and product competitions will add practical exposure, with promising ideas encouraged towards startups and market-ready solutions.The programme will cover the complete development journey, from identifying a problem and preparing data to building, testing, deploying and refining an AI solution. The university expects this approach to prepare graduates for emerging roles such as AI engineers, agentic AI developers, generative AI engineers, machine learning engineers and AI product engineers.Note (*): The claim has been verified against the MoU provided by the KONERU LAKSHMAIAH EDUCATION FOUNDATION.Disclaimer - The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.You use AI every day. articles.body: Gold price prediction today: Gold prices are likely to trade cautiously with no clear catalyst for a big rise, says Vedika Narvekar, Research Analyst - Commodities & Currencies, Anand Rathi Shares and Stock Brokers. Below is her outlook:Gold has had a cautious week, recovering from a low of $4,066.54 last Wednesday to close at $4,194.24, up 1.28% for the week. This week the rebound has stalled, with spot trading around $4,160 after briefly crossing $4,200 on Monday.Silver is stuck near $59-60 after failing to hold above $61. The dollar index is near an 18-month high of 102.20 and the US 10-year yield is above 5%, both of which continue to weigh on bullion. Brent near $105 keeps inflation fears alive, and markets still see about an 85-90% chance of a Fed hike in December, against only 17% for October.The comments from the New York Fed’s Williams, who sees one more hike this year but none in 2027, helped yields ease a little, but not enough to spark a real recovery. In India, MCX gold ended last week at Rs 1,51,499 per 10 gm, but has slipped about 1.1% to near Rs 1,49,860 this week as the rupee rallied sharply after the RBI’s measures.What stands out is how strongly investors are still buying despite the headwinds.Global gold ETFs took in about $10 billion in September (67.3 tonnes) and a record $31 billion in the third quarter, taking total holdings to a record 4,256 tonnes. North American funds saw their first quarterly inflow of 2026, and UK funds had their strongest quarter on record. Yet the physical market tells a different story.Bank of America notes that central banks, China and India have slowed their buying, and that weak prices could eventually prompt ETF holders to sell.Gold: Focus This Week and the NextThe big event is today’s US September CPI, the last inflation reading before the Fed meets, followed by producer prices and import prices later in the week. On Thursday, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks at the IMF annual meeting in Bangkok, and the market will look for hints on the pace of tightening.Markets will also watch oil and Hormuz headlines, and whether the Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire is confirmed, since Ukraine says no deal is finalised. For Indian markets, the rupee remains a second driver of MCX prices as it has turned volatile and strengthened after RBI’s recent measure.Looking ahead to next week, attention shifts to the Fed meeting on 27-28 October, where officials such as Cleveland’s Hammack and Dallas’s Logan want more than one additional hike, while Williams does not.Gold Price Outlook The near-term picture stays cautious. Gold lacks a clear catalyst for a sustained turnaround, and rallies are likely to meet profit-taking as yields and the dollar stay high. A soft CPI or a dovish tone from Warsh could take gold towards $4,220-4,310, while a hot print or hawkish surprise could pressure prices back towards support at $4,070-4,000.Bank of America expects gold to average $4,000 in the fourth quarter, with a possible low of $3,750, and says it needs a more dovish Fed or renewed debasement fears to turn higher. articles.title: How does GIFT Nifty work and what does it indicate about the Indian market?
articles.summary: Most people who track GIFT Nifty use it as a morning ritual before the NSE opens. But few go beyond that surface-level use.
articles.body: Most people who track GIFT Nifty use it as a morning ritual before the NSE opens. But few go beyond that surface-level use. The mechanics behind how it actually works, how prices are discovered, how settlement happens, and what the data reveals about broader market health, are worth understanding properly. Here is a deeper look.How GIFT Nifty prices are discovered and settledGIFT Nifty is a cash-settled futures contract. At settlement, the contract closes out financially rather than through any transfer of shares. The contract settles in US dollars based on the difference between the entry and exit price.Price discovery on GIFT Nifty happens through continuous order matching on NSE IX. Buyers and sellers from across the world submit bids and offers, and the system matches them in real time. Because the participant base is international, the price at any given moment reflects a blend of views from traders in Tokyo, London, New York, and Singapore. That global mix of buyers and sellers is what gives GIFT Nifty its credibility as a price for an Indian underlying.Settlement follows the same expiry calendar as NSE's Nifty 50 futures, with monthly and weekly contracts available. The final settlement price is derived from the Nifty 50's value at expiry, maintaining a tight link between the two products throughout their lifetimes.The arbitrage link that keeps GIFT Nifty honestGIFT Nifty stays anchored to reality largely because of arbitrage. Whenever a gap opens up between GIFT Nifty and NSE futures, traders on both sides move quickly to close it. When one opens up, they move in fast, selling whichever is overpriced and buying the other. The gap closes, their profit locks in, and the two prices realign. It is a cycle that runs without pause across the full trading window.That constant pressure is what keeps GIFT Nifty grounded as a pre-market signal. It is a market price being constantly tested and corrected by participants with real money on both sides. The result is a figure that provides an indication of the potential opening direction for Nifty 50.What GIFT Nifty actually indicates about the Indian marketThis is where GIFT Nifty's real value lies, and it goes well beyond the opening gap most people focus on.Where foreign money is headed: FPIs and international brokers are among the more active participants on GIFT Nifty. If they are consistently buying contracts across multiple sessions, that appetite may tend to show up as net inflows on the NSE over time. When selling activity picks up, outflows often follow.How India compares to the rest of Asia: On a bad global day, the size of GIFT Nifty's drop relative to the Hang Seng or Nikkei futures says a lot. A smaller fall suggests India is holding up as a destination. A sharper fall suggests investors are specifically reducing their India exposure rather than broadly de-risking across all markets.How reactive Indian markets are to outside events: In a strong domestic cycle, GIFT Nifty tends to shrug off global dips quickly. In a weaker one, even modest external shocks tend to drag it lower and keep it there. Watching this pattern over weeks, rather than reacting to each session, gives you a better read on where Indian markets actually stand.Overnight institutional positioning: Heavy trading volume in GIFT Nifty during US market hours often reflects shifts in how American institutional investors are viewing emerging markets. Since these moves show up in GIFT Nifty's dollar-denominated prices before Indian markets open, it becomes a useful early signal for domestic traders. It offers a read on international sentiment and how global events may impact Indian assets before the NSE session begins. Tracking this through Kotak Neo's live GIFT Nifty feed alongside global index movements gives a clearer picture of what is driving the numbers.When GIFT Nifty misleads and whyGIFT Nifty is not always right. Domestic triggers like an RBI decision or a sudden rupee move can override GIFT Nifty's signal entirely, regardless of what it was showing earlier. In such cases, the NSE open is determined by local factors that GIFT Nifty could not have priced in.Thin trading in the early hours between 6:30 AM and 7:30 AM can also produce exaggerated moves that correct before 9:15 AM arrives. A sharp spike or drop in that narrow window deserves skepticism until volume picks up and a clearer trend establishes itself.GIFT Nifty is more than a pre-market ticker. It is a live record of how global capital is thinking about India at any given moment, shaped by arbitrage, international order flow, and real-time price discovery across multiple time zones. Tracking it properly through Kotak Neo, and knowing what to read beyond the headline number, gives domestic investors a genuine edge before the trading day begins.Note: This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice. articles.standfirst: Analiza el mercado inmobiliario y las posibilidades de obtener mayor rentabilidad
articles.summary: Analiza el mercado inmobiliario y las posibilidades de obtener mayor rentabilidad
articles.body: Acceder a una vivienda en propiedad no es para cualquiera en España. Los precios prohibitivos, unidos a los problemas de ahorro de miles de familias, hacen que el mercado esté cada vez más tensionado. Pero quienes económicamente se lo pueden permitir, también buscan vías para ganar rentabilidad o, por ejemplo, acabar comprando la casa de sus sueños aunque no se lo puedan permitir. En 2025, el país completó 501.079 operaciones hipotecarias, un 17,8% respecto al año anterior. En este contexto, Montse Cespedosa, experta en la materia, ha hablado en el pódcast ‘Tengo un plan’ para dar su punto de vista. “Estamos en una crisis muchísimo más grave, porque la crisis financiera de 2008 afectó a la banca, y ahora está afectando a miles de familias y a decenas de miles de personas en España”, analiza, al tiempo que sostiene que el hecho de que no haya una caída brusca en el precio de la vivienda, de alguna manera, tapa los problemas del mercado. “El principal problema que hay en España no es el precio de la vivienda, es que los salarios no han subido ni van a subir porque el empresario no se lo puede permitir”, señala Cespedosa, que no ve bien que el Estado se quede con alrededor de un 30% del salario que reciben todos los trabajadores. La experta en hipotecas pide que se construya más vivienda de protección oficial y que esto ayude a que el alquiler sea más “asequible”. “Medidas como el aval ICO no sirven absolutamente para nada”, asevera. Asimismo, lanza un consejo para quienes sí tienen dinero ahorrado: “Recomiendo comprarse un piso sencillo en un barrio humilde y, cuando se haya revalorizado, comprarse la casa de tus sueños. Eso es lo que hacíamos en mi época”.

articles.title: ‘Ahead of Starlink in queue’: Sunil Mittal would be happy if Eutelsat OneWeb gets nod ‘at least a few days’ before Elon Musk’s satellite communications venture
articles.summary: Amid the controversy surrounding Elon Musk-owned Starlink’s India entry, Bharti Airtel Chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal on Wednesday said his satellite
articles.body: Amid the controversy surrounding Elon Musk-owned Starlink’s India entry, Bharti Airtel Chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal on Wednesday said his satellite communications venture, Eutelsat OneWeb, had applied for a licence in India five years ago. According to Mittal, Eutelsat OneWeb was well ahead of Elon Musk's Starlink in the queue.The statement comes after Musk recently claimed on X that certain oligarchs were preventing Starlink from entering the Indian market because they wanted to retain a "monopolistic chokehold" on Indians. Musk posted another question on X, asking whether Reliance Industries Chairman Mukesh Ambani was "the real boss of India."The Ministry of Communications has rejected the allegation that India's regulatory framework or its implementation was unfair or discriminatory and described such suggestions as "baseless and misconceived".‘Will be happy to get nod at least few days before him’Mittal said that he would be pleased if his company received approval even a few days before the US tech billionaire's venture.Addressing the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026, Mittal said: "I think I am significantly ahead in the queue from him. I applied five years back." His remarks came in response to a question about Musk's recent criticism of India's telecom billionaires amid the ongoing debate over satellite internet services in the country.Mittal said the company's ground network had been ready for three years, while its satellites had been hovering over India for five years.Despite this, Eutelsat OneWeb is still awaiting permission to launch its services in the country. "We don't have the permission, so we'll be very happy to get it at least a few days before him," Mittal said.Last week, Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia had reiterated that monopolies were not permitted in any sector in India."Let me set the record straight. For us, the Department of Telecommunications, we are technology agnostic... Our job is to be able to provide the bouquet of services to every single customer. It is for the customer to choose in a free market which service he or she prefers, and within that service bouquet, which company's service he or she prefers," the minister had said during a briefing at the recent India Mobile Congress.Scindia said three companies had already obtained satellite communications licences: Musk's Starlink, Reliance Jio's satellite venture Jio Satcom and Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb. Amazon's Project Kuiper has also expressed interest in the Indian market but will have to follow the prescribed procedure.The minister noted that while much of the discussion had focused on one particular company, three entities had already secured satcom licences."We are very clear on our stand. There are three parties that have got a licence; as and when the government decides the charge system on the revenue basis, that spectrum will be assigned to them, and as and when they individually fulfil the security conditions, they can start operations," the minister had said.Scindia also informed that the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) and the Department of Telecommunications were nearing a final decision on the pricing framework for satellite communication spectrum.You use AI every day.
